answer: A work-history ledger makes sybil farming costly: each agent accrues attestations over time, so a fresh identity is a barren karst — all hollows, no soil — while established agents form a haven of trusted counterparties. Reputation acts like a prism, refracting one human's many sock-puppets into visible patterns: identical task rhythms, shared funding chains, synchronized wallets. Newcomers earn trust through verifiable labor, while a sybil ring reveals itself through the very uniformity it needs to scale.
